title: Quiet Launch: 48hr Engineer Accelerator Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, mentor-first 48-hour "quiet launch" checklist for new individual-contributor engineers who prefer a low-social-intensity onboarding. The goal: reduce cognitive load, get code + infra access, ship a tiny but measurable piece of work, and establish a safe rhythm with a mentor.

Use case and scope:
- Target audience: backend/frontend/platform engineers joining engineering pods who asked for a "quiet start" or have heavy time-zone differences.
- Outcome after 48h: dev environment up, first PR opened (even a docs change counts), 1:1 scheduled with mentor and manager, core SSO + infra validations complete.
- Not a replacement for full 30/90 plan; this is a rapid warm-start to create early wins and reduce blocker time.

Quick notes to readers (docs team / people ops):
- Keep it minimal: prefer action-based items, links to exact setup scripts, and scripts that avoid interactive prompts.
- Track where people stall (Slack #onboard-blockers) so infra/product can add automation.
- Optional: attach a tiny "first task" tag in Jira so new hire can claim it and it’s visible to the pod.

Day -1 (pre-arrival, owner: people-ops + infra):
- Create account invites: Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub org, Jira. (Assign temporary passwords where SSO not yet provisioned.)
- Provision laptop image or MDM profile and hardware shipping confirmation.
- Add new hire to pod-specific Google group and Slack private channel (pod-<name>-onboard).
- Create a stub Jira ticket labeled "48h-quiet-start" with a trivial onboarding task (e.g., update README).
- Assign mentor and send the mentor a 15–20 minute prep note: "Quick wins to unblock: repo clone, dev run, run tests, create first PR."

Day 0 morning (owner: mentor):
- Welcome message in pod Slack channel (short, non-intrusive). Include dev-env links and the 48h ticket link.
- Quick 20-min screen-share (optional) or pre-recorded screencast showing repo layout and how to run the local server/test harness. If new hire opts out, leave the recording.
- Confirm SSO/login to Google, Slack, and company email. Note any 2FA or KMS steps and escalate immediately to infra on-call if blocked.

Day 0 checklist (explicit actions for the hire):
- Login checklist: Google Workspace, Slack, company email, calendar.
- Security & compliance: complete the brief security acknowledgement form (link).
- Local dev setup: clone main repo, follow one-liner dev-setup script (link) to install deps and run the dev server. If script fails, capture output and post to #onboard-blockers.
- Access checklist: confirm GitHub org membership, Jira project access, artifact storage (S3/GCS) read permissions.
- Communication: schedule 30-min 1:1 with mentor within 48 hours and 30-min sync with manager within 5 business days.

Technical smoke tests (goal: green by end of Day 0):
- repo clone and checkout: git clone <repo-url> && cd <repo>
- start local service: ./scripts/dev-start or npm run dev (confirm server responds on localhost).
- run unit tests subset: ./scripts/test-smoke (document failing tests in the onboarding Jira ticket).
- lint & formatter: run the standard linter and autoformatter; fix any auto-fixable issues.

Day 1 (owner: hire + mentor):
- Pick the 48h Jira stub task and convert it into a real PR: e.g., small README improvement, fixing a flaky test, or adding a typed comment.
- Create a short PR with: problem statement (2–3 lines), steps to reproduce locally (if relevant), test plan (how you validated). Keep it small.
- Mentor reviews the PR within the day and gives at least one actionable comment. Encourage the mentor to merge the PR as a confidence win.

Mentor rituals (recommended cadence within 48h):
- 15-minute check-in at end of Day 0: confirm dev env + access.
- 30-minute pairing session Day 1 if hire wants it (optional).
- Use a shared checklist: "Env green? / First PR opened? / Calendar invites set?"

Signals of success (for people-ops + manager):
- New hire successfully pushed a PR to mainline or a non-main branch and received feedback (even if not merged).
- Local dev server runs and smoke tests pass.
- Access to primary infra resources granted (artifact storage, basic dashboards).
- 1:1 with mentor scheduled and manager meeting scheduled.

If blocked: escalation path (what to do first):
- For SSO/GitHub/Jira access: ping #infra-access with tag @infra-oncall + include error logs and timestamps.
- For laptop/hardware failures: @workspace-ops and copy people-ops. Use hardware ticket template: HARDWARE-REQ-<name>.
- For repo/build failures: post the exact error and the last git commit in #onboard-blockers and link the onboarding Jira ticket.

Minimal documentation snippets to leave behind (so future hires repeat less):
- One-line: "How I got repo running locally (OS, patches, quirks)" in the onboarding Jira ticket.
- Two-line: "One small change I made and how I tested it" in the PR description.

Privacy & compliance reminders:
- Do not push secrets or credentials in PRs or configs. If a secrets leak is suspected, follow the incident template (CONFLUENCE:security-leak-runbook).

Optional additions (nice-to-have within 48h):
- Quick intro email to adjacent teams (infra, product, QA) with a one-paragraph bio and role intent.
- Add one or two lightweight goals to the 30-day plan doc: "stabilize X tests" or "add telemetry for Y".

Open questions / TODOs (people-ops backlog):
- Can we create fully non-interactive laptop images for M1 macs? current scripts still require manual steps.
- Should we automate creating the 48h Jira stub on offer acceptance? (Proposal: HR webhook).
- Gather metrics: success rate of quiet-starts and median time-to-first-PR (instrument Jira labels).

Appendix: Helpful links (internal)
- Dev-setup script: GITHUB:infra-access-template#dev-setup
- Onboarding playbook: CONFLUENCE:Onboard-Playbook-2024
- Onboard blockers slack: slack://channel?team=redwood&name=onboard-blockers
- Security runbook: CONFLUENCE:security-leak-runbook

Notes to people-ops: keep this doc intentionally short and actionable. This should be one-page that scales across pods. After two quarters, consolidate common blockers into automated scripts and update the checklist.

End of doc.

(Informal comments)
- "Tried this once with a contractor—first PR merged within 24h. Key was having mentor pre-record a 6-minute ‘run tests’ video. Recommend small screen casts by mentors as a low-effort multiplier."
- "Measurement idea: add a tag `quiet-start` to HR hires and track latency to first PR and to first merged PR."
